title: Inferential Statistics: T-Test, ANOVA, MANOVA, ANCOVA
summary: Parametric tests; significance; test power; effect size; independent/paired/one-sample t-test; degrees of freedom; one-way/two-way/repeated-measures ANOVA; post hoc; MANOVA; ANCOVA.
revision: Parametric tests assume normality, homogeneity, interval/ratio, independence. t-test = two means; ANOVA = three+ means. Power = avoiding Type II error. Effect size = magnitude.
traps: ANOVA requires three or more groups.
confusions: Using t-test for more than two groups.
Confusing statistical significance with practical significance.

i: Interval or ratio scale of measurement.

notes.t: The likelihood that an observed result is not due to chance, typically p < 0.05.
The probability of correctly rejecting a false null hypothesis (avoiding Type II error).

r: Compare one sample mean to a known value
Compare same group before and after

i: MANOVA — multiple dependent variables analysed simultaneously.
ANCOVA — ANOVA with a covariate to control extraneous variance.

notes.t:
Worked example: Independent t-test. Group A (n=10, M=75, SD=5), Group B (n=10, M=70, SD=5).
Pooled SD ≈ 5. Standard error ≈ 5 × √(2/10) ≈ 2.24.
t = (75 − 70) / 2.24 ≈ 2.23. With df = 18, p < 0.05 → significant.
Interpretation: Group A scored significantly higher than Group B.
t-test compares two means; ANOVA compares three or more. Post hoc tests locate differences after significant ANOVA. Effect size (Cohen's d, η²) is increasingly tested.

mnemonics.title: TAPME
mnemonics.text: T — t-test (two means), A — ANOVA (three+ means), P — Post hoc (after ANOVA), M — MANOVA (multiple DVs), E — Effect size (magnitude).

flashcards.a: Comparing three or more group means.
Larger sample size, larger effect, smaller variance.
